title: Serengeti Sopa Lodge Is Now Serengeti Explorer, and the Hilltop View Is Still the Point
meta_title: Serengeti Sopa Lodge, Rebuilt as Serengeti Explorer
meta_description: Serengeti Sopa Lodge reopened in 2025 as Serengeti Explorer. Rooms, location, park fees and who it suits, from a Nairobi safari team.
excerpt: Serengeti Sopa Lodge was rebuilt on its Nyaboro Hills site and reopened as Serengeti Explorer by Elewana. Here is what changed, how to get there and what a night really costs.
content:
Serengeti Sopa Lodge no longer trades under the Sopa name: the old lodge on the Nyaboro Hills was knocked down and rebuilt on the same site, and it reopened in January 2025 as Serengeti Explorer by Elewana. It keeps the hilltop views and the central location, with new rooms, a 35-metre pool and far more to do on site.

That matters if you are comparing quotes, reading older reviews or looking at an itinerary that still lists the lodge by its former name. Below we explain what changed, where the lodge sits, how to reach it, what a night really costs once park fees are added, and who it suits on a Tanzania safari through the Serengeti.

Quick Facts

  • Former name: Serengeti Sopa Lodge; reopened as Serengeti Explorer by Elewana in January 2025
  • Location: Nyaboro Hills, south-central Serengeti National Park, south-west of Seronera
  • Rooms: 68 Explorer rooms and six suites, the same count as the old lodge
  • Getting there: About an hour's flight from Arusha to Seronera airstrip, then roughly 45 minutes by road
  • Park fees: US$82.60 entry per adult per 24 hours from 16 May to 14 March (checked November 2026)
  • Best for: Families, first-timers and travellers who want lodge comforts in the middle of the park

What Happened to Serengeti Sopa Lodge?

Serengeti Sopa Lodge was one of the oldest lodges in the central Serengeti. Its owners demolished the original building and put up a new lodge on the same footprint, which opened in January 2025 under Elewana Collection's new Explorer brand. The hill and the view stayed; almost everything else at Serengeti Sopa Lodge is new.

The Sopa group confirms the change in its August 2026 newsletter, which says the Serengeti and Ngorongoro properties "were rebranded to Explorer by Elewana Collection" and Tarangire Sopa Lodge is now the group's only Tanzanian property. According to the owner's opening announcement, the room count was deliberately kept the same as before so the rebuild would not add pressure on the surrounding ecosystem.

Is Serengeti Sopa Lodge still open?

The building is open, but under a new name. If you search for Serengeti Sopa Lodge on a map, a booking engine or an older guidebook, you will usually land on Serengeti Explorer. Reviews dated before 2025 describe a building that no longer exists.

Some itineraries, including a few of ours, still list Serengeti Sopa Lodge "or similar" because that is how the name is recognised. When we confirm a booking, we tell you exactly which property you are staying in, whether that is the rebuilt lodge or a comparable one if it is full on your dates.

What about Ngorongoro Sopa Lodge?

Ngorongoro Sopa Lodge, on the eastern rim of the crater, is part of the same rebrand according to the Sopa newsletter, but we could not find a confirmed reopening date for it at the time of writing. If your trip includes the crater, our guide to Ngorongoro Crater lodges compares the rim, highland and Karatu options so you have a fallback.

Where Is the Lodge, and How Do You Get There?

The lodge sits high on the Nyaboro Hills in the south-central Serengeti, south-west of Seronera, the park's central hub. Most guests either fly from Arusha to Seronera airstrip and drive about 45 minutes, or arrive by road on a Northern Circuit safari after Ngorongoro.

The hill is why guests loved Serengeti Sopa Lodge and why the rebuild kept the site: open plains in several directions, so game viewing starts at breakfast. The trade-off is that every drive begins with a short descent to the main tracks.

RouteTypical timeNotes
Arusha to Seronera by light aircraftAbout 1 hourScheduled flights; luggage limits on small planes are strict
Seronera airstrip to the lodgeAbout 45 minutesThe 2023 pre-opening FAQ said 75 minutes, so allow extra time for game on the way
Arusha to the central Serengeti by roadAbout 7 hoursUsually split with a night near Ngorongoro
Ngorongoro Crater rim to the lodgeHalf a dayCrosses the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, which charges its own transit fee

Road safaris crossing the Ngorongoro Conservation Area pay a transit fee of US$70.80 per adult per 24 hours, usually twice, set by the Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority (checked November 2026). Fly-in guests to Serengeti Sopa Lodge skip it but need a vehicle and guide waiting at Seronera.

Rooms, Food and the Pool at the Rebuilt Lodge

Serengeti Explorer has 68 Explorer rooms and six suites, each with a private balcony facing the plains. Some rooms connect for families and two are built for wheelchair users. A 35-metre pool anchors the main area.

Rooms and suites

The pre-opening FAQ describes the standard room at about 46 square metres with an en-suite bathroom, a daybed on the balcony, a tea and coffee station, a safe and a charging board with USB and USB-C points. Suites add a lounge, a bathtub and butler service. No air conditioning is listed; the FAQ mentions standing fans, which suits the cool hilltop nights. Check the latest details on Serengeti Explorer's official page before you book.

Where you eat

Breakfast is in the Acacia restaurant and lunch at the Kisimani pool bar. Evenings bring an outdoor Boma dinner or a wine-paired meal in the Divai cellar, both usually extra. A lobby deli packs food for long game drives.

Families and accessibility

Families are well looked after on the old Serengeti Sopa Lodge site, better than at most Serengeti camps. The FAQ lists interconnecting rooms, family suites, a supervised bushcraft centre for ages 4 to 12 and babysitting from two years. Bush walks start at 16. Our Tanzania family safari guide explains how to pace a Serengeti trip with children.

What Can You Do Without Leaving the Lodge?

Serengeti Explorer offers more on-site activity than the old Sopa did: a photographic hide beside a waterhole, guided bush walks, free stargazing with a resident astronomy guide, an outdoor cinema and a spa. Away from the lodge, the main extra is ranger-led rhino tracking in the Moru Kopjes.

The Moru Kopjes are granite outcrops south of the lodge where lions often rest on the warm rock and the park keeps a small, protected black rhino population. Rhino are never guaranteed, but this is one of the few places in the Serengeti where you have a real chance.

Bush walks from Serengeti Sopa Lodge (now Explorer) take up to six guests for two to three hours and cost extra. Stargazing is the quiet highlight: the central Serengeti has almost no light pollution, and it is free for guests.

When Is the Best Time to Stay at Serengeti Sopa Lodge?

The central Serengeti around Serengeti Sopa Lodge has resident lions, leopards, cheetahs and plains game all year, so there is no bad month. The migration herds usually pass through the central and western areas between April and June, and again around November and December as they head back south.

MonthsWhat to expect near the lodgeWho it suits
December to MarchHerds mostly in the south around Ndutu; resident predators stay centralTravellers combining calving season in the south with a central base
April to mid-MayLong rains; lowest park entry of US$70.80; some roads muddyBudget-minded travellers who do not mind rain
Late May to JulyHerds move through the centre and west towards the Grumeti; dry season beginsMigration seekers who also want comfort
August to OctoberHerds mostly in the far north near the Mara River; centre quieter but cats reliableFirst-timers happy to stay central for predators
NovemberShort rains; herds drift south through the east and centreShoulder-season value before the festive rush

Migration timing moves with the rain each year, so treat these as patterns rather than promises. Our great migration month by month guide tracks where the herds usually are, and the best Serengeti camps guide covers bases in the north and south if you want to follow them more closely.

How Much Does a Night Cost Once Park Fees Are Added?

A night at Serengeti Sopa Lodge costs the room rate plus park fees. Tanzania National Parks (TANAPA) lists entry at US$82.60 per adult per 24 hours (US$70.80 from 15 March to 15 May) and a concession fee of US$59 per adult per night, or US$70.80 from July to September (checked November 2026).

Children aged 5 to 15 pay less and under-fives enter free. Safari quotes often include these fees, so check yours, and confirm the figures before booking as TANAPA revises its tariff.

When the lodge opened, the owner's opening announcement gave rack rates of US$900 to US$1,450 per room per night on full board (two adults and one child under 12), or US$1,380 to US$1,930 on a game package with drives. Those are launch figures from March 2025, so treat them as a guide to the price band and ask for today's rate.

Insider Tips

  • Search both names: Use Serengeti Explorer as well as the old name when you read reviews, and ignore anything from before 2025
  • Ask about the drive package: If you fly in, the game package adds drives and saves arranging a separate vehicle
  • Book rhino tracking early: Moru Kopjes outings depend on rangers and space, so request them with your booking
  • Pack layers: Mornings on the hill are cool, and the FAQ lists fans rather than air conditioning
  • Check the fees line: Make sure your quote names park entry, concession and Ngorongoro transit fees

Who Should Book This Lodge, and Who Should Look Elsewhere?

The rebuilt Serengeti Sopa Lodge suits families, first-time visitors, groups and anyone who wants a pool, varied dining and accessible rooms in the middle of the park. It suits less well if you want a small tented camp, total quiet, or to sit beside the migration in the far north from August to October.

With 74 rooms, Serengeti Sopa Lodge was always large by Serengeti standards and the rebuild is no different, so expect company at breakfast and by the pool. Few small camps match its kids' centre or accessible rooms, but if you would rather hear lions than neighbours, we can suggest an intimate tented camp.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Serengeti Sopa Lodge the same as Serengeti Explorer?

Yes. Serengeti Sopa Lodge was demolished and rebuilt on the same Nyaboro Hills site, then reopened in January 2025 as Serengeti Explorer by Elewana. The location and the room count stayed the same, but the rooms, restaurants, pool and activities are all new, so older reviews of the Sopa building no longer describe what you will find.

How do you get to Serengeti Sopa Lodge?

Most guests reach Serengeti Sopa Lodge, now Serengeti Explorer, by flying about an hour from Arusha to Seronera airstrip and driving roughly 45 minutes to the lodge. On a road safari it is about seven hours from Arusha, usually split with a night near Ngorongoro, and the route crosses the Ngorongoro Conservation Area.

Is the lodge good for families with children?

Serengeti Explorer is one of the more family-friendly bases in the Serengeti. It has interconnecting rooms, family suites, a supervised bushcraft centre for children aged 4 to 12 and babysitting from two years old. Guided bush walks are only for guests aged 16 and over, so plan other activities for younger children on those mornings.

What park fees do you pay when staying in the central Serengeti?

Staying at a lodge inside the Serengeti means paying park entry of US$82.60 per adult per 24 hours for most of the year, or US$70.80 from mid-March to mid-May, plus a concession fee of US$59 to US$70.80 per night. These were checked in November 2026 on TANAPA's site and should be confirmed before booking.

When is the best month to stay at the lodge?

The central Serengeti has resident predators and plains game all year, so any month works. For migration herds nearby, aim for late May to July or around November and December, when the wildebeest usually pass through the centre and west. April and early May are cheapest but bring the long rains and muddier roads.

Final Thoughts

The lodge many travellers still call Serengeti Sopa Lodge is now the rebuilt Serengeti Explorer, with the same superb hilltop position. It is a strong choice for families and first-timers who want comfort and a central base in this UNESCO World Heritage Site, rather than a small camp following the herds.
